node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e places offering in Scope. node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 place promotional conditions in Scope. Failed conditions return OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed negative or compliant answer. This conflicts with a question covering all assessed benefits or offers, but could implement an expressly narrower assessment domain; that alternative remains unresolved.

The offer-level candidates combine offer-wide promotion with the existence of a non-discount gift without expressly requiring that the same gift have the promotional connection. Mixed offers could be overclassified unless the supplied facts establish that connection.
The circular supports an SFC-authorised-fund assessment context. It does not establish that paragraph 3.11 applies only to those funds.

Gift classification remains a supplied judgment: paragraph 9 says returns or incentives may be gifts. Neither guaranteed-return status nor underlying-fund-return provenance alone establishes prohibition or exemption. Passing the gift control does not establish disclosure, advertising or section 103 compliance.
